_derivation: Every tolerance here comes from measured convergence, not from an observed
error rounded up. The reference settings are grid 64^3, alpha 0.35 1/A,
real-space cutoff 8.0 A, GMD B-spline order 6 against OpenMM's fixed order 5.
RE-DERIVED after the electrostatic constant was corrected from 14.3996 to
the CODATA 2022 value 14.3996454686836 (+3.157635e-06 relative). Every
measurement below was taken again from the regenerated reference. They are
unchanged to four significant figures, and the tolerances land on the same
numbers, because the constant multiplies GMD and the rescaled external
results identically -- it cancels from the comparison. What the correction
moved is the absolute energies and forces, not the agreement between codes.
At those settings each code's own mesh error, measured against the exact
Ewald sum (same alpha, same cutoff, kmax 24):
GMD order 6    energy 1.974117e-07 eV   max force 2.691640e-07 eV/A
OpenMM order 5 energy 9.338915e-07 eV   max force 1.262620e-06 eV/A
Two implementations of a mesh method can differ by at most the sum of their
distances from the exact answer, so the triangle-inequality bound is
energy 1.131303e-06 eV   max force 1.531784e-06 eV/A.
The observed differences are 1.131303e-06 and 1.531784e-06: the bound is
tight to every digit, not loose, because the two codes deviate from exact
Ewald in opposite directions. The tolerances below are that bound doubled,
which leaves room for round-off differences between platforms while staying
orders of magnitude below any real regression -- for scale, the
reciprocal-force bug fixed in commit b9b7493 produced a force error of
8.9e-02 eV/A, and the constant correction itself moved every Coulomb
quantity by 3.16e-06 relative.
Convergence tolerances are the mesh error at grid 64 doubled. Wrapped
equivalence is exact up to floating-point representation of x +/- L, so its
tolerance is set near double-precision round-off rather than by measurement.
Translation by a non-lattice vector is NOT exact for a mesh method; its
tolerance is the grid-64 mesh error doubled.
_net_force: A mesh method does not conserve momentum exactly: the grid is fixed to the
box, so translational invariance is broken at the mesh-error level and the
net force is nonzero by construction. Measured at grid 64: GMD 1.616e-07,
OpenMM 7.550e-07 eV/A. It shrinks with refinement exactly as the mesh error
64, 128), so the tolerance is set from that measurement, not from zero.
Exact Ewald has no mesh and so does conserve momentum to round-off, which
is why it gets a tolerance five orders tighter.
_independence_floor: The reference must NOT be GMD's own output. Two different PME
implementations at different interpolation orders cannot agree bitwise, so
a difference at or below this floor means the checked-in reference was
replaced with something GMD generated. The observed difference is 1.13e-06
in energy and 1.53e-06 in force, both a hundred times this floor.
